title: Retire the worker registry's tier enum
action: Slice 5, D4 (store 97ce5225). bee state worker add and worker update carry --tier with the same closed three-value enum the cell verb had (workers.rs:86-101, :125-127, :147-150, :187-193). role is the sole model selector now, so a worker row records the ROLE its dispatch resolved, not a cost tier. Decide and state on the cap whether the field is renamed on the worker row or simply stops being enum-checked — the row is written by dispatch prepare and read by the cap door's registered-worker check, so a rename touches both and a bare de-enum touches neither. Whichever you choose, an existing worker row written before this change must still satisfy the cap door; a migration that strands in-flight workers would refuse correct caps. Sibling cells own the cells verb (mrs-15) and the accounting (mrs-17) — leave their files alone. Run your verify with --no-fail-fast: the repo's declared command lacks it and aborts at the first failing target, so without it your own target may never run.

truths: No closed three-value enum constrains what a worker row records
A worker row written before this change still satisfies the cap door's registered-worker check
The cap states whether the field was renamed or de-enumed, and why
